Package com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.vision

Class LimelightBotpose

java.lang.Object
com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.vision.LimelightBotpose
public final class LimelightBotpose extends Object
The format of a Limelight's botpose array, in one place.

The simulator writes it and the fusion reads it, so defining it twice would be asking for the two to stop matching one day with nothing to warn you. A test makes the round trip between the two halves of the feature so that cannot happen silently.

The format

 [0..5]   x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw      metres and degrees
 [6]      total latency                  milliseconds
 [7]      tag count
 [8]      tag span                       metres
 [9]      average camera-tag distance    metres
 [10]     average area                   percentage of the image
 [11+]    7 values per tag               id, txnc, tync, ta, distCamera, distRobot, ambiguity

The tag block is only filled in if the length is exactly 11 + 7 * tagCount. It is the same condition LimelightHelpers imposes, and the reason the published tag count has to match the tags actually appended.

  • Method Details

    • parse

      public static Optional<LimelightBotpose.Estimate> parse(double[] raw, long ntTimestampMicros, boolean megaTag2)
      Parses a botpose array.

      The capture timestamp comes from the NetworkTables clock minus the latency. It is worth knowing that this is the local clock, not serverTime: that is why a Limelight source is dated correctly even when the publisher lives in the same process, which is not the case for QuestNav.

      Parameters:
      raw - the array exactly as it comes out of NetworkTables.
      ntTimestampMicros - the instant NetworkTables received the value, in microseconds.
      megaTag2 - whether it comes from a botpose_orb key.
      Returns:
      the estimate, or empty if the array is empty or too short.
